item.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
item.description:
Skim new method — GNN-based region scoring CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the best baseline across 324 quantum circuits on the TianYan-176 processor. Reusing the trained model with updated calibration data preserves the highest mean fidelity across six dates without retraining.

Grade 0.503 · 2.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Noise-Adaptive Compiler Mappings for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Computers” · Wenjie Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Zhigang Wang, Yuchen He, Shengbin Wang, Hantao Sun

Figure

Bar chart comparing the mean measurement-distribution fidelity across seven benchmark datasets for CREST and four baseline methods on TianYan-176.

Asks

How can quantum compilation select execution subregions on superconducting processors to optimize circuit-specific execution fidelity while remaining robust across recalibrations without retraining?

Before

Baseline compilation methods QSteed, SABRE, and HAQA. On the 96 held-out circuit benchmark, mean fidelity was 0.18100 (HAQA) versus 0.21347 with CREST.

But

Evaluated on a single superconducting device architecture (TianYan-176) across circuits up to 20 qubits; offline candidate graph precomputation required.

Tools

Graph neural network (GNN) scoring · Bidirectional cross-graph attention · TianYan-176 superconducting processor · Multiscale candidate region construction

Abstract

Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. It encodes gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions alongside each candidate region's connectivity and current calibration attributes; bidirectional cross-graph attention relates the two representations, while real-device execution outcomes supervise candidate ranking. The trained scorer is reused with updated calibration attributes. Evaluations on 324 circuits from seven datasets on TianYan-176 show that CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the strongest baseline and achieves the highest mean fidelity on every dataset. Furthermore, using updated calibration attributes, the same trained model maintains the highest overall mean fidelity across six measurement dates without retraining. With a unified model of circuit-region compatibility, CREST improves execution fidelity across diverse workloads and sustains that advantage as hardware calibration changes.

arxave:action.title: Assess transfer to spin-qubit calibration and connectivity

item.arxave:action: Map CREST's circuit-region scoring inputs to the spin-qubit device's calibration schema (gate fidelities, readout, coherence, connectivity) and test whether the approach can rank execution regions for the 16+ qubit spin QPU.
Ask which calibration attributes are required by the trained scorer, how often they must be refreshed, and whether the model can be reused when only a subset of qubit/pair parameters changes.

arxave:action.title: Superconducting-trained model may not transfer directly

item.arxave:action: The evaluation is on TianYan-176 superconducting hardware; spin-qubit noise, connectivity, and calibration drift may differ enough that the scorer needs retraining or a new feature set before operational use.
